cat: Rereading the EPR paper from 1935 - Einstein really thought he had them cornered.
Wigner's friend is the thought experiment I always use to start the measurement-problem lecture.
Heisenberg's microscope argument is so much shakier than the textbooks make it sound.
Bohr's reply to EPR is famously hard to parse, even for physicists.
Everett's 1957 thesis still reads as radical today.
teapot: Russell's 'Why I Am Not a Christian' lecture came up again in seminar today.
Pascal's wager is still the argument students find most annoying.
Flew's parable of the invisible gardener is a great way into falsifiability.
Paley's watchmaker argument is older than people think.
Hume's Dialogues are the best thing written on the design argument.
butterfly: The Cook Ding passage in the Zhuangzi, carving the ox along its natural joints - still my favourite.
Zhuangzi's useless tree story is the best defence of doing nothing I know.
The happiness-of-fish debate with Huizi on the bridge over the Hao is such a good exchange.
Reading the Daodejing alongside the Zhuangzi this term.
Zhuangzi drumming on a pot after his wife died - that passage still shocks students.
crane: Our class visited the Peace Memorial Museum in Hiroshima again this August.
We folded paper boats for Toro Nagashi on the river last summer.
Tanabata wishes on bamboo were always my favourite school activity.
The orizuru diagrams in my first origami book were so hard to follow.
We always made kabuto paper helmets for Children's Day.
tortoise: Zeno's arrow paradox - at every instant the arrow is at rest.
The dichotomy paradox is the one that convinces students limits matter.
Cantor's diagonal argument still feels like magic every time I teach it.
Hilbert's hotel is the easiest way into infinite sets.
The sorites paradox came up in seminar - when does a heap stop being a heap?
cave: Republic Book VI - the divided line is so much harder to teach than people think.
The ring of Gyges in Book II is the best opener for an ethics course.
The ship of state analogy in the Republic still feels topical.
Rereading the Symposium - Diotima's ladder of love.
The myth of Er at the end of the Republic is so strange.
rosebud: The breakfast-table montage in Citizen Kane is the best marriage story in two minutes.
Gregg Toland's deep focus in Kane changed cinematography for good.
The Third Man's sewer chase is the best ending Welles was ever part of.
Touch of Evil's opening tracking shot is still unbeatable.
Kane's 'News on the March' newsreel sequence is a brilliant parody.
moth: Darwin's finches in the Galapagos are still the classic adaptive radiation example.
The Grants' work on beak size during the 1977 drought is beautiful field biology.
Lenski's long-term E. coli experiment just passed another milestone.
Antibiotic resistance is the cleanest real-time selection example for students.
The Galapagos tortoise shell shapes are a nice example of island adaptation.
